rationale: The agent verified identity via the user’s email and matched it to a single account before proceeding. It reviewed both orders with read-only tools, confirmed the user’s intent to return all items and asked which refund methods to use. The user explicitly specified the refund mapping (#W5490111 to Visa, #W7387996 to PayPal), and the agent executed returns accordingly using the appropriate tool, with results reflecting the requested refund methods. The agent then provided accurate confirmation of what was submitted. When the user objected and requested the opposite mapping after submission, the agent explained it could not change the refund method post-submission (no tool exists to modify return refund methods) and offered a handoff to a human, which it completed. There were no unauthorized actions, no actions on another account, and no unsupported claims about order details. A minor nit is that the agent did not restate the exact changes for a final “Are you sure?” confirmation before writing, but the user’s explicit instruction sufficed as confirmation in context. Overall, the agent acted within policy and completed the request appropriately, then escalated when requirements changed.
